title: GPU Dropout Diagnostics - Juno & Zhen
description: Every signal that could explain the RTX 5090 Xid-79 dropouts on Juno and Zhen. Established mechanism: deaths ride host power TRANSIENTS (400-1900W steps) - not thermals, and not PCIe signal integrity (zero AER and zero PCIe replays in 70 days). Junction temperature is the newest and least-proven signal: check the Monitoring health row before trusting it. RESOLUTION: Prometheus scrapes at 60s, so nothing here can show sub-minute behaviour; the 5Hz telemetry ring and incident bundles on each host are the only sub-second record.

panels.title: GPUs visible
panels.description: DCGM keeps reporting a dead GPU, so a drop here means the driver lost it entirely. Zhen should be 5; Juno should be 5 but is currently 4 - 01:00.0 is dead pending a power cycle.

panels.title: XID now
panels.description: Non-zero = a GPU raised an Xid. 79 = 'fallen off the bus'.

panels.title: Chassis power
panels.description: BMC DCMI whole-chassis draw. The established death mechanism is a STEP in this value, not a high level.

panels.title: PSU total out
panels.description: Sum of PSU output from the local PMBus exporter, which sees PSUs the BMC cannot.

panels.title: Max junction
panels.description: Vendor: sustained >=100C under a DEFINED load = due for service. A legitimate soak reaches 100-110C, so never read this without load context.

panels.title: 12V rail (min)
panels.description: Power-delivery hypothesis: a sag here coincident with a power step is the smoking gun to look for.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Short uptime after an unexplained gap means the HOST went down, not just a GPU.

panels.title: Exporters down
panels.description: If non-zero, panels below may be blank for reasons unrelated to hardware.

options.content:
**Established (do not re-litigate):** deaths ride host power **transients** (400-1900W steps); *ruled out* are PCIe signal integrity (zero AER, zero replays in 70 days), PCIe switches (none exist - direct root ports), ambient/diurnal timing, and PSU shelf state as a sole cause. Card **349f61c8** accounts for 14 of 27 deaths across two hosts and four slots - track cards by **UUID, never by slot**.

**Workflow after a death:** find the red XID annotation, then read *Power transients* and *12V rail* at that timestamp, then *Active throttle reasons*. Temperature has never distinguished the bad card - survival time under load did.

**Two limits to keep in mind.** (1) Scrape interval is 60s, so no panel here can show sub-minute rail behaviour - the host's 5Hz ring at `/var/log/gpu-recorder/telemetry.csv` and the incident bundles are the only sub-second record. (2) Junction temperature comes from a third-party BAR0 register offset whose 5090 profile is upstream-**experimental**; a gap in the junction series means *rejected or stale*, not cool. Check the **Monitoring health** row before drawing a conclusion from it.

panels.title: Power delivery - the established death mechanism
Per-GPU power draw
panels.description: 10 of 11 resolvable deaths sat on a 400-1900W host power step. Look for one card's draw stepping hard, or all cards ramping together.

panels.title: Power budget: GPUs vs PSU output vs chassis
panels.description: Three independent measurements of the same power. Divergence between them is itself a finding - e.g. PSU output far exceeding GPU draw means something else is loading the rails.

panels.title: Power TRANSIENTS (5m change in total GPU draw)
panels.description: THE key panel: deaths correlate with steps of 400-1900W. Spikes here - in either direction - are the events to line up against the red XID annotations. RESOLUTION CAVEAT: Prometheus scrapes these hosts every 60s, so a 1m window contains a single sample and this panel can only show minute-scale steps. Genuine sub-second rail transients are invisible here and exist ONLY in the recorder's 5Hz ring on the host (/var/log/gpu-recorder/telemetry.csv) - do not conclude 'no transient' from this panel alone.

panels.title: 12V rail voltage
panels.description: Zoom in hard. A dip at the instant of a power step supports the power-delivery hypothesis; a flat rail through a step weakens it.

panels.title: Per-PSU output power
panels.description: Uneven sharing, or one PSU dropping its share, points at a specific unit. PSU faults here followed the HARDWARE across slots, not the slot.

panels.title: PSU status OK (0 = fault)
panels.description: Necessary but not sufficient: a host ran 10,849 minutes on a degraded shelf with ZERO deaths, so a fault here does not by itself explain a dropout.

panels.title: All board rails
panels.description: VCPU/VSOC/VCCM are the CPU and DRAM rails. A correlated wobble across several rails suggests an upstream (PSU/input) cause rather than one failing regulator.

panels.title: PSU input voltage & current
panels.description: Mains-side view. A sag in INPUT voltage during a load step means the problem is upstream of the PSUs entirely.

panels.title: Junction & thermals - newest signal, verify before trusting
Junction (hotspot) temperature
panels.description: From BAR0 MMIO - no NVIDIA interface reports this. Only emitted when the reading passes the validity gate, so a GAP means rejected or stale, NOT cool. 95C warn, 100C service.

panels.title: Junction - core delta
panels.description: Best long-term 'is this card degrading' metric. Both operands share one instant. At CONSTANT power a rising trend means thermal-interface degradation (pump-out, dried paste). Compare a card against its own history, not against its siblings.

panels.title: Core temperature (two independent sources)
panels.description: gputemps vs NVML. These must agree within ~3C - that agreement is what proves junction readings are attributed to the right card. Divergence invalidates the junction panels above.

panels.title: GDDR max (two independent BAR readers)
panels.description: gddr6_* and gpu_vram_* are separate implementations reading the same sensors. They agree within 0-2C, which is the strongest evidence that the BAR mapping and 5090 profile are correct.

panels.title: Thermal margin (T.Limit) - LOWER IS HOTTER
panels.description: NVIDIA's official margin. Measured to be exactly 90 - core on these cards, so it adds nothing over core temperature - but it is the designated fallback if junction ever proves untrustworthy. Alert on LOW values.

panels.title: Per-module GDDR temperature (all modules)
panels.description: 8 modules per card. One module consistently hotter than its siblings is a localised cooling problem (pad contact) rather than a whole-card issue.

panels.title: XID errors
panels.description: 79 = 'GPU has fallen off the bus'. 31 = memory/illegal address. 154 = recovery action. Each occurrence is also annotated across every panel on this dashboard.

panels.title: PCIe replay counter (5m increase)
panels.description: RULED OUT as a cause: zero replays on every GPU for 70 days, and zero AER through 40+ minutes of maximum DMA. Kept because any non-zero value here would overturn that conclusion.

panels.title: Active throttle reasons
panels.description: HW-THERMAL / HW-SLOWDOWN firing at only 77-82C core is the anomaly that motivated the junction work. KEY CHECK: if HW-THERMAL asserts while junction reads ~80C, the junction offsets are WRONG.

panels.title: SM & memory clocks
panels.description: A clock collapse without a throttle reason, or clocks pinned low after an event, indicates the card never recovered.

panels.title: Load context - what the cards were actually doing
Utilisation & engine activity
panels.description: There were NO idle deaths. Establishing what the card was doing at the moment of death is essential context for any thermal or power claim.

panels.title: PCIe throughput
panels.description: Heavy sustained DMA is the condition the C-Payne stress tool reproduces. Useful for correlating a death with bus activity.

panels.title: Framebuffer used
panels.description: A large resident footprint means the GDDR modules are genuinely being exercised, which matters when reading the VRAM temperatures above.

panels.title: Chassis & board temperatures
panels.description: 'Card Side Temp' is the closest thing to a GPU inlet reading. Ambient was RULED OUT as a driver of death timing, but inlet temperature is still required context for any junction service claim.

targets.expr: ipmi_temperature_celsius{host=~"$host",name=~"CPU Temp|MB Temp|Card Side Temp|Onboard LAN Temp|TEMP_TR1"}

panels.title: Chassis fan speeds
panels.description: Driven by gpu-fan-control (20% floor, 50% ceiling over 70-85C core). A fan stuck high often means it is tracking a DEAD GPU's frozen temperature - that exact bug has happened here.

panels.title: DIMM temperatures
panels.description: Zhen has an outstanding 8th-DIMM issue. A MISSING sensor here is as informative as a hot one.

panels.title: PSU temperature & fans
panels.description: A PSU running hot, or with a stalled fan, can trip protection under a load step without ever reporting a hard fault.

panels.title: Host load & memory
panels.description: Rules out the host itself stalling as the cause of an apparent GPU disappearance.

panels.title: BMC SEL log count
panels.description: The BMC event log records hardware faults the OS never sees. A step here at the time of a death is a strong lead - Juno's full SEL is an outstanding action, and a full log stops recording new events.

panels.title: Monitoring health - READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING JUNCTION
panels.description: junction_temp_valid 0, map_trusted 0, reader_up 0, or a rising parse_errors all mean the junction panels above are not reporting reality. The 5090 profile in the upstream tool is EXPERIMENTAL and was never maintainer-tested on a 5090.

panels.title: GPU inventory - identify a card across hosts and slots
panels.description: Card 349f61c8 accounts for 14 of 27 deaths across two hosts and four slots, so always track a card by UUID, never by slot.
